h: I will make you a great nation

p: אִיתָא בַּגְּמָרָא (פְּסָחִים קיז עַמּוּד ב):
It is taught in the Gemara (Pesachim 117b):
"'וְאֶעֶשְׂךָ לְגוֹי גָּדוֹל' – זֶה שֶׁאוֹמְרִים אֱלֹהֵי אַבְרָהָם;
''And I will make you a great nation'—this is why we say 'God of Avraham';
'וַאֲבָרֶכְךָ' – זֶה שֶׁאוֹמְרִים אֱלֹהֵי יִצְחָק;
'and I will bless you'—this is why we say 'God of Yitzchak';
'וַאֲגַדְּלָה שְׁמֶךָ' – זֶה שֶׁאוֹמְרִים אֱלֹהֵי יַעֲקֹב;
'and I will make your name great'—this is why we say 'God of Yaakov';
יָכוֹל יְהוּ חוֹתְמִין בְּכוּלָּם? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: 'וֶהְיֵה בְּרָכָה' – בְּךָ חוֹתְמִין וְכוּלֵי".
might one think they conclude with all of them? Scripture states: 'and you shall be a blessing'—with you they conclude, etc.'

h: I will make you a great nation

p: וּבַזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ אִיתָא:
And in the holy Zohar it is stated:
"'וְאֶעֶשְׂךָ לְגוֹי גָּדוֹל' – בְּגִין דִּכְתִיב 'לֶךְ לְךָ';
''And I will make you a great nation'—because it is written 'Go for yourself';
'וַאֲבָרֶכְךָ' – בְּגִין דִּכְתִיב 'מֵאַרְצְךָ';
'and I will bless you'—because it is written 'from your land';
'וַאֲגַדְּלָה שְׁמֶךָ' – בְּגִין דִּכְתִיב 'וּמִמּוֹלַדְתְּךָ';
'and I will make your name great'—because it is written 'and from your birthplace';
'וֶהְיֵה בְּרָכָה' – בְּגִין דִּכְתִיב 'וּמִבֵּית אָבִיךָ'.
'and you shall be a blessing'—because it is written 'and from your father's house.'
רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אָמַר: 'וְאֶעֶשְׂךָ לְגוֹי גָּדוֹל' – מִסִּטְרָא דִימִינָא;
Rabbi Shimon said: 'And I will make you a great nation'—from the right side;
'וַאֲבָרֶכְךָ' – מִסִּטְרָא דִשְׂמָאלָא;
'and I will bless you'—from the left side;
'וַאֲגַדְּלָה שְׁמֶךָ' – מִסִּטְרָא דְאֶמְצָעִיתָא;
'and I will make your name great'—from the central pillar;
'וֶהְיֵה בְּרָכָה' – מִסִּטְרָא דְאַרְעָא דְיִשְׂרָאֵל.
'and you shall be a blessing'—from the side of the Land of Israel.
הָא הָכָא כּוּרְסַיָּא דְאַרְבַּע סַמְכִין דְּכֻלְּהוּ כְּלִילָן בֵּיהּ בְּאַבְרָהָם".
Behold here the Throne of four supports, all of which are included within Avraham.'

h: The Zohar’s teaching and spiritual perfection

p: הִנֵּה כָּל דִּבְרֵיהֶם הַקְּדוֹשִׁים מְרַמְּזִין עַל עִנְיָן אֶחָד,
Behold, all their holy words allude to one unified theme,
עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתַב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ: "לֶךְ לְךָ וְכוּלֵי – לְאַתְקָנָא דַּרְגָּא דִילָךְ",
based on what is written in the holy Zohar: ''Go for yourself, etc.—to rectify your spiritual rung,'
וְהַיְינוּ כִּי אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ הָיְתָה מִדָּתוֹ חֶסֶד שֶׁהוּא עִנְיַן הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת,
meaning that Avraham our Father's attribute was Chesed, which is the quality of outward expansion,
וְהִשְׁתַּדֵּל לְפַרְסֵם כְּבוֹד אֱלֹהוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת רַב בְּכָל הָעוֹלָם;
and he exerted himself to publicize the glory of His divinity with vast expansion across the entire world;
וְלָכֵן גִּיֵּיר גֵּרִים הַרְבֵּה לְהַכְנִיס כָּל הָעוֹלָם תַּחַת כַּנְפֵי הַשְּׁכִינָה.
and therefore he converted many proselytes to bring the entire world beneath the wings of the Shechinah.
וְאָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: "לֶךְ לְךָ" מֵאוֹתוֹ הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת שֶׁבֵּין הָאוּמּוֹת,
And the Holy One said to him: 'Go for yourself' out of that diffuse expansion among the nations,
כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת כָּל הַגֵּרִים שֶׁגִּיֵּיר חָזְרוּ לְסוּרָם אַחַר פְּטִירָתוֹ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בְּפִרְקֵי דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר פֶּרֶק כט, עַיֵּין שָׁם),
for in truth, all the converts he made reverted to their corruption after his passing (Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer 29, see there),
וְהַיְינוּ הַגֵּרִים שֶׁגִּיֵּיר בְּאֶרֶץ חָרָן, כְּמַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וְאֶת הַנֶּפֶשׁ אֲשֶׁר עָשׂוּ בְחָרָן", וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה.
referring to the converts he made in Charan, as stated: 'and the souls that they had gotten in Charan' (Genesis 12:5), and as written in Bereishit Rabbah.
וּכְנֶגֶד זֶה "וְאֶעֶשְׂךָ לְגוֹי גָּדוֹל" –
And corresponding to this He said: 'And I will make you a great nation'—
וְהַיְינוּ הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת הַקְּדֻשָּׁה בְּזַרְעֲךָ,
meaning the expansion of holiness within your own seed,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה: "אוֹתָהּ אֻמָּה שֶׁכָּתוּב בָּהּ: 'כִּי מִי גוֹי גָּדוֹל', אֲנִי מַעֲמִיד מִמְּךָ".
and as written in Bereishit Rabbah: 'That nation of whom it is written: 'For what nation is there so great' (Deuteronomy 4:7), I will establish from you.'
וְזֶה כַּוָּנַת הַגְּמָרָא: "זֶה שֶׁאוֹמְרִים אֱלֹהֵי אַבְרָהָם",
And this is the meaning of the Gemara: 'this is why we say God of Avraham,'
כִּי שְׁלֹשָׁה תָּאֳרֵי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ "הַגָּדוֹל, הַגִּבּוֹר וְהַנּוֹרָא" נֶגֶד קְדֻשַּׁת הָאָבוֹת;
for the three divine titles 'the Great, the Mighty, and the Awesome' correspond to the holiness of the Patriarchs;
וְ"הַגָּדוֹל" הַיְינוּ הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת, וְזֶה מִצַּד הַגְּדוּלָּה וְהַחֶסֶד.
and 'the Great' signifies expansion, stemming from Gedulah and Chesed.
וְזֶהוּ גַּם כֵּן מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר "מִסִּטְרָא דִימִינָא", וְהַהִתְגַּלּוּת עַל יְדֵי אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ, עַיֵּין שָׁם.
And this is likewise what the Zohar means by 'from the right side,' its revelation occurring through Avraham our Father, see there.

paragraphs.text: Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer 29:9: “Rabbi Jochanan said: All heathens who come to Israel are circumcised by their own freewill and with their consent, and in the fear of Heaven are they circumcised. We do not believe a proselyte until seven generations (have passed), so that the waters should not return to their source. But slaves are circumcised both by their freewill and with their consent as well as without their consent, and no confidence is placed in slaves. Likewise with all the slaves who were circumcised with our father Abraham, they did not remain true (converts) in Israel, neither they nor their seed, because it is said, "All the men of his house, those born in the house, and those bought with money of the stranger, were circumcised with him" (Gen. 17:27). Why did he circumcise them? Because of purity, so that they should not defile their masters with their food and with their drink, for whosoever eateth with an uncircumcised person is as though he were eating flesh of abomination. All who bathe with the uncircumcised are as though they bathed with carrion, and all who touch an uncircumcised person are as though they touched the dead, for in their lifetime they are like (the) dead; and in their death they are like the carrion of the beast, and their prayer does not come before the Holy One, blessed be He, as it is said, "The dead praise not the Lord" (Ps. 115:17). But Israel who are circumcised, their prayer comes before the Holy One, blessed be He, || like a sweet savour, as it is said, "But we will bless the Lord from this time forth and for evermore. Praise ye the Lord" (Ps. 115:18).”

h: Blessing and abundance and the forefathers

p: "וַאֲבָרֶכְךָ" נִרְמַז עַל יִצְחָק אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
''And I will bless you' is hinted regarding Yitzchak our Father, peace be upon him,
וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וַאֲבָרֶכְךָ – בְּגִין דִּכְתִיב מֵאַרְצְךָ",
and this is why it says: ''and I will bless you'—because it is written 'from your land','
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁנִּצְטַוָּה לָצֵאת מֵהַהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת שֶׁלּוֹ אֶל הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר אַרְאֶךָּ,
meaning that he was commanded to withdraw from that diffuse expansion and go toward the land that I will show you,
שֶׁזֶּה מְרַמֵּז עַל יִצְחָק שֶׁלּוֹ נֶאֱמַר: "גּוּר בָּאָרֶץ הַזֹּאת";
which hints at Yitzchak, unto whom it was explicitly commanded: 'Sojourn in this land' (Genesis 26:3);
וּמִדַּת יִצְחָק הוּא הַצִּמְצוּם,
and the attribute of Yitzchak is contraction (Tzimtzum),
שֶׁרָאָה שֶׁמִּכָּל גִּיּוּרֵי אָבִיו לֹא נִשְׁאַר, שֶׁחָזְרוּ לְסוּרָם,
for he saw that of all the converts of his father none remained, having reverted to their ways,
וְלָכֵן צִמְצֵם קְדֻשָּׁתוֹ שֶׁלֹּא לְהִתְפַּשֵּׁט בֵּין עוֹבְדֵי כוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת,
and therefore he contracted his holiness so as not to expand among the nations,
וְלָכֵן לֹא כְּתִיב בְּיִצְחָק שֶׁגִּיֵּיר גֵּרִים,
and therefore it is not written regarding Yitzchak that he made converts,
רַק בְּרֶמֶז חֲכָמֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת וַיֵּשֶׁב):
except in the subtle allusion of our Sages (Bereishit Rabbah, Parashat Vayeishev):
"בְּאֶרֶץ מְגוּרֵי אָבִיו – מִגִּיּוּרֵי אָבִיו",
''In the land of his father's sojournings (megurei)'—from his father's converts (giyurei),'
כִּי מְעַט הָיוּ הַגֵּרִים שֶׁגִּיֵּיר,
for few were the converts he made,
שֶׁלֹּא גִּיֵּיר רַק יְחִידִים שֶׁהֵבִין שֶׁלֹּא יַחְזְרוּ לְסוּרָם.
converting solely distinct individuals of whom he discerned that they would never relapse.
וְזֶה שֶׁאוֹמְרִים "אֱלֹהֵי יִצְחָק" – מִדַּת "הַגִּבּוֹר",
And this is why we recite 'God of Yitzchak'—corresponding to the attribute 'the Mighty',
דִּגְבוּרָה הִיא מִדַּת צִמְצוּם.
for Gevurah is the attribute of contraction.
וּמְרַמֵּז בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ: "וַאֲבָרֶכְךָ – מִסִּטְרָא דִשְׂמָאלָא",
And it is hinted in the holy Zohar: ''and I will bless you'—from the left side,'
שֶׁמָּצִינוּ בּוֹ בְּרָכָה מְפוֹרֶשֶׁת: "וַיִּמְצָא בַּשָּׁנָה הַהִוא מֵאָה שְׁעָרִים וַיְבָרֲכֵהוּ ה'",
for regarding him we find an explicit blessing: 'And he found in that year a hundredfold, and Hashem blessed him' (Genesis 26:12),
כִּי מִדַּת הַצִּמְצוּם שָׁם צָרִיךְ לִבְרָכָה.
for within the attribute of contraction blessing is especially essential.
וְגַם לְהַמִּדְרָשׁ שֶׁהוּבָא בְּרַשִּׁ"י: "'וַאֲבָרֶכְךָ' – בְּמָמוֹן",
And also according to the Midrash cited in Rashi: ''and I will bless you'—with wealth,'
זֶהוּ מִמִּדָּתוֹ, דִּכְתִיב: "מִצָּפוֹן זָהָב יֶאֱתֶה",
this stems from his attribute, as written: 'Out of the north comes gold' (Job 37:22),
וְשֶׁיַּעֲשִׁיר יַצְפִּין, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא כה עַמּוּד ב);
and he who desires to become rich should face north, as written (Bava Batra 25b);
וּבְיִצְחָק נֶאֱמַר: "כִּי גָדַל מְאֹד",
and of Yitzchak it is said: 'for he grew exceedingly great' (Genesis 26:13),
שֶׁאָמְרוּ: "זֶבֶל פִּרְדוֹתָיו וְלֹא כַּסְפּוֹ וּזְהָבוֹ שֶׁל אֲבִימֶלֶךְ",
such that the Sages said: 'The dung of his mules, and not the gold and silver of Avimelech,' (Bereishit Rabbah 64),
דְּכָל כָּךְ הָיָה עָשְׁרוֹ בְּהַפְלָגָה, כְּמַשְׁמָעוּת לְשׁוֹן "מְאֹד" דִּקְרָא.
so extraordinary was his vast wealth, as indicated by the term 'exceedingly' in the verse.

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 84:4: “Another matter: “Jacob settled…” – Abraham converted proselytes. paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Tiferet Yosef, Sukkot 11: ““Isaac sowed in that land and found in that year a hundredfold, and the Lord blessed him.” Isaac’s quality is might. From the standpoint of the kindness that the blessed God established in this world, the flow appears to reach even those who transgress His will, as the Talmud says that rain falls for everyone, righteous and wicked alike. Isaac’s quality limits the flow so that it goes only to those who perform God’s will. Because of this limitation, it reaches them with great force. This is the meaning of the Sages’ question, “What are the mighty powers of rain?”—because rain descends with might. Through this quality, the flow descends with tremendous force. Therefore Isaac’s blessing, “Who revives the dead,” includes all salvations: supporting the fallen, healing the sick, and so forth. Isaac’s limitation is this: in this world, the Zohar describes the kingdom as having no eyes. Thus the Talmud says: if someone steals a measure of wheat and sows it, by rights it should not grow, but the world follows its customary course. This is called having no eyes. In truth, one who looks deeply into this quality sees that it too has eyes. One who serves God, trusts in the Life of worlds, and sows receives what proceeds from God’s mouth within the good, giving that good life and existence. One who remains only at the surface receives only the garment of the good, without its inwardness. Whoever looks deeply sees this, although on the surface both appear to receive the same good. This is the world following its customary course. Isaac illuminates that there is judgment and a Judge; whoever says the Holy One, blessed be He, simply waives judgment forfeits his life. Through this quality he limits the flow so that even the outer garment of the good reaches only those who do His will. The good therefore comes to them with great force. This is “Isaac sowed in that land and found in that year a hundredfold,” rendered as a hundred times the estimated yield: through Isaac’s quality, those who do God’s will receive the flow with great force.”

הנה מדתו של יצחק הוא מדת הגבורה. כי מצד מדת חסדו ית' שהציב השי"ת בזה העולם נדמה שהולכת ההשפעה גם לעוברי רצונו. כעין דאיתא בש"ס (תענית ז'.) מטר לכל בין לצדיקים ובין לרשעים, ורק מצד מדת יצחק מגביל ההשפעה שתלך רק לעושי רצונו של מקום, ומחמת זאת ההגבלה, נמצא שהולכת ההשפעה לעושי רצונו בגודל תוקף. וזה כוונת חז"ל (שם ב'.) מאי גבורות גשמים אמר ר"י מפני שיורדין בגבורה והוא כנ"ל, כי מצד זאת המדה הולכת ההשפעה בזעף גדול. ומפני זה בברכת יצחק שהוא מחיה מתים נכללים כל הישועות, סומך נופלים ורופא חולים וכו'. וענין זה הגבלה של יצחק אע"ה הוא, כי באמת בעוה"ז נקרא בזוה"ק (משפטים צ"ה) מדת מלכות לית לה עיינין. כמו דאיתא בש"ס (ע"ז נ"ד:) הרי שגזל סאה חטים וזרעה בקרקע בדין הוא שלא תצמח אלא עולם כמנהגו נוהג, וזה נקרא לית לה עיינין. ובאמת מי שמעמיק במדה הזאת רואה, שגם במדה הזאת אית לה עיינין. והיינו מי שהולך בעבודה ומאמין בחי עולמים וזורע באמת מקבל המוציא פי ד' המונח בהטובה המחיה והמהוה את הטובה. ומי שהוא רק על הגוון, אינו מקבל רק הלבוש מהטובה בלי שום פנימיות. וזה הכל מי שמעמיק רואה זאת, אבל על הלבוש נדמה שזה מקבל טובה כמו זה, וזה נקרא עולם כמנהגו נוהג. וזה ענין של יצחק אע"ה שמאיר בזה העולם אית דין ואית דיין, שכל האומר הקב"ה ותרן יותרו חייו (ב"ק נ'.) ובזאת המדה מגביל ההשפעה שאפילו הלבוש מהטובה ג"כ לא יקבל רק עושי רצונו, נמצא שמצד זאת ההגבלה הולך הטובה לעושי רצונו בכח גדול. וזה ויזרע יצחק בארץ ההוא וימצא בשנה ההוא מאה שערים ומתרגם מאה בדשערוהי, והיינו שמצד מדתו מקבלין עושי רצונו ההשפעה בכח גדול:
reviewedSourceExcerpt.en: “Isaac sowed in that land and found in that year a hundredfold, and the Lord blessed him.” Isaac’s quality is might. From the standpoint of the kindness that the blessed God established in this world, the flow appears to reach even those who transgress His will, as the Talmud says that rain falls for everyone, righteous and wicked alike. Isaac’s quality limits the flow so that it goes only to those who perform God’s will. Because of this limitation, it reaches them with great force. This is the meaning of the Sages’ question, “What are the mighty powers of rain?”—because rain descends with might. Through this quality, the flow descends with tremendous force. Therefore Isaac’s blessing, “Who revives the dead,” includes all salvations: supporting the fallen, healing the sick, and so forth. Isaac’s limitation is this: in this world, the Zohar describes the kingdom as having no eyes. Thus the Talmud says: if someone steals a measure of wheat and sows it, by rights it should not grow, but the world follows its customary course. This is called having no eyes. In truth, one who looks deeply into this quality sees that it too has eyes. One who serves God, trusts in the Life of worlds, and sows receives what proceeds from God’s mouth within the good, giving that good life and existence. One who remains only at the surface receives only the garment of the good, without its inwardness. Whoever looks deeply sees this, although on the surface both appear to receive the same good. This is the world following its customary course. Isaac illuminates that there is judgment and a Judge; whoever says the Holy One, blessed be He, simply waives judgment forfeits his life. Through this quality he limits the flow so that even the outer garment of the good reaches only those who do His will. The good therefore comes to them with great force. This is “Isaac sowed in that land and found in that year a hundredfold,” rendered as a hundred times the estimated yield: through Isaac’s quality, those who do God’s will receive the flow with great force.

h: Unto the land that I will show you

p: וְגַם "אֶל הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר אַרְאֶךָּ" שֶׁמְּרַמֵּז עַל יִצְחָק,
And also 'unto the land that I will show you' alludes to Yitzchak,
שֶׁלֹּא מָצִינוּ בַּפָּסוּק שֶׁהֶרְאָהוּ, רַק הַכַּוָּנָה "שֶׁאֶתְרָאֶה לְךָ",
for we do not find that He pointed it out to him, but the meaning is 'wherein I will appear unto you,'
דְּהַנְּבוּאָה בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל.
for authentic prophecy manifests in the Land of Israel.
וְהַגַּם דְּאָז עֲדַיִן לֹא נִבְחֲרָה אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל,
And although at that time the Land of Israel had not yet been uniquely designated,
וְאִיתָא בְּרֵישׁ הַמְּכִילְתָּא: שֶׁהָיוּ אָז כָּל אֲרָצוֹת כְּשֵׁרוֹת לְדִבְּרוֹת,
and it is taught at the beginning of the Mekhilta that until then all lands were valid for divine utterances,
וְהָיוּ רְאוּיוֹת אָז לְהַשְׁרָאַת שְׁכִינָה,
and were then eligible for the dwelling of the Shechinah,
וְכֵן בָּא אֵלָיו מַאֲמַר ה' "לֶךְ לְךָ" בְּחוּץ לָאָרֶץ;
and indeed Hashem's utterance 'Go for yourself' came to him in the Diaspora;
מִכָּל מָקוֹם לְשׁוֹן "וַיֵּרָא" לֹא נֶאֱמַר אֶלָּא אַחַר כָּךְ מִיָּד שֶׁבָּא לְאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל לִשְׁכֶם.
nevertheless, the expression 'and He appeared' was uttered only afterward immediately upon arriving in the Land of Israel at Shechem.
וְגַם מִדַּת הַיִּרְאָה – פַּחַד יִצְחָק:
Furthermore, the attribute of Fear is the Fear of Yitzchak:
עַל יְדֵי שֶׁיִּתֵּן אֶל לִבּוֹ שֶׁמֶּלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עוֹמֵד עָלָיו וְרוֹאֶה בְּמַעֲשָׂיו,
through placing upon his heart that the King of kings stands over him and sees his deeds,
מִיָּד יַגִּיעַ אֵלָיו הַיִּרְאָה וְהַפַּחַד;
fear and awe immediately overcome him;
וּפַחַד יִצְחָק הַיְינוּ שֶׁרוֹאֶה שֶׁעוֹמֵד לִפְנֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ,
and the Fear of Yitzchak means beholding that one stands before the King.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּגְּמָרָא (שַׁבָּת פט עַמּוּד ב): "וּמַחְוֵי לְהוּ יִצְחָק הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בְּעֵינַיְיהוּ",
And this is what they taught (Shabbat 89b): 'And Yitzchak points out the Holy One before their very eyes,'
וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר "אֲשֶׁר אַרְאֶךָּ" – שֶׁאֶתְרָאֶה אֵלֶיךָ.
and this is 'that I will show you'—wherein I will appear unto you.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Kometz HaMinchah 2:53:1: ““Lest you take my son back there.” Awe comes from nearness: when one stands before the king, one fears him, as stated in the gloss at the beginning of Orach Chayim. Likewise, “with great awe” is the revelation of the Divine Presence. Love, by contrast, can be stronger at a distance, as in the familiar example of a son whose longing for his father increases when he is far away. The Land of Israel is the level of “I have set God before me always,” and “a land upon which the eyes of the Lord your God always rest.” Outside the Land, one is described as like someone who has no God—that is, not directly before his eyes, but at a distance. This is the meaning of “The air of the Land of Israel makes one wise.” The Sages use the word wise for recognition—as in, “Does the Master recognize Rav Pappa?”—since recognition comes from wisdom; the Land’s air brings forth the recognition of divinity, and recognition comes from nearness. Therefore Abraham warned against taking Isaac outside the Land, where there is no place for this awe, but rather love. This is what Shabbat 89b says: Isaac shows them the Holy One, blessed be He, with their own eyes. “They will see eye to eye,” and setting God directly before one’s eyes, are Isaac’s level. The capacity for this also comes through Isaac’s quality: might is restriction, through which God, as it were, limits the spread of His light so that even the lowliest person can apprehend it. As is known, “God is your shadow”: God’s response corresponds to a person’s level. When the person fears and restricts himself, so does God. It says “with their eyes,” as in “They will see eye to eye,” because awe purifies sight, as explained earlier. As Avodah Zarah says, the vessels of the eye depend on the heart, and awe is associated with the heart, as Yoma explains the verse, “But there is no heart.””

reviewedSourceExcerpt.en: “Lest you take my son back there.” Awe comes from nearness: when one stands before the king, one fears him, as stated in the gloss at the beginning of Orach Chayim. Likewise, “with great awe” is the revelation of the Divine Presence. Love, by contrast, can be stronger at a distance, as in the familiar example of a son whose longing for his father increases when he is far away. The Land of Israel is the level of “I have set God before me always,” and “a land upon which the eyes of the Lord your God always rest.” Outside the Land, one is described as like someone who has no God—that is, not directly before his eyes, but at a distance. This is the meaning of “The air of the Land of Israel makes one wise.” The Sages use the word wise for recognition—as in, “Does the Master recognize Rav Pappa?”—since recognition comes from wisdom; the Land’s air brings forth the recognition of divinity, and recognition comes from nearness. Therefore Abraham warned against taking Isaac outside the Land, where there is no place for this awe, but rather love. This is what Shabbat 89b says: Isaac shows them the Holy One, blessed be He, with their own eyes. “They will see eye to eye,” and setting God directly before one’s eyes, are Isaac’s level. The capacity for this also comes through Isaac’s quality: might is restriction, through which God, as it were, limits the spread of His light so that even the lowliest person can apprehend it. As is known, “God is your shadow”: God’s response corresponds to a person’s level. When the person fears and restricts himself, so does God. It says “with their eyes,” as in “They will see eye to eye,” because awe purifies sight, as explained earlier. As Avodah Zarah says, the vessels of the eye depend on the heart, and awe is associated with the heart, as Yoma explains the verse, “But there is no heart.”

paragraphs.text: Tanya, Likkutei Amarim 41:2–4: “That is, he should at least contemplate in his mind the greatness of the blessed Infinite One and His kingship, which is “the kingship of all worlds,” higher and lower. He “fills all worlds” and “encompasses all worlds,” as it is written, “Do I not fill heaven and earth?” Yet He sets aside the higher and lower worlds and directs His kingship particularly toward His people Israel as a whole, and toward this person individually, for a person is obligated to say, “For my sake the world was created.” He, for his part, also accepts His kingship upon himself: that He should be King over him, and that he should serve Him and perform His will through every kind of a servant’s service. Behold, Hashem stands over him; “the whole earth is filled with His glory.” He looks upon him and examines his innermost parts and heart to see whether he serves Him properly. He must therefore serve before Him with awe and fear, like someone standing before the king. He should deepen this thought and dwell upon it according to the capacity of his mind and thought, and according to the time available to him, before engaging in Torah or a mitzvah—for example, before putting on a tallis and tefillin.”

reviewedSourceExcerpt.en: That is, he should at least contemplate in his mind the greatness of the blessed Infinite One and His kingship, which is “the kingship of all worlds,” higher and lower. He “fills all worlds” and “encompasses all worlds,” as it is written, “Do I not fill heaven and earth?” Yet He sets aside the higher and lower worlds and directs His kingship particularly toward His people Israel as a whole, and toward this person individually, for a person is obligated to say, “For my sake the world was created.” He, for his part, also accepts His kingship upon himself: that He should be King over him, and that he should serve Him and perform His will through every kind of a servant’s service. Behold, Hashem stands over him; “the whole earth is filled with His glory.” He looks upon him and examines his innermost parts and heart to see whether he serves Him properly. He must therefore serve before Him with awe and fear, like someone standing before the king. He should deepen this thought and dwell upon it according to the capacity of his mind and thought, and according to the time available to him, before engaging in Torah or a mitzvah—for example, before putting on a tallis and tefillin.

p: "וַאֲגַדְּלָה שְׁמֶךָ – בְּגִין דִּכְתִיב וּמִמּוֹלַדְתְּךָ",
''And I will make your name great'—because it is written 'and from your birthplace',
וְזֶה שֶׁאוֹמְרִים "אֱלֹהֵי יַעֲקֹב",
and this is why we say 'God of Yaakov',
כִּי "וַאֲגַדְּלָה שְׁמֶךָ" מְרַמֵּז עַל יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם.
for 'and I will make your name great' alludes to Yaakov our Father, peace be upon him.
כִּי שֵׁם כָּל דָּבָר מוֹרֶה עַל הַחַיּוּת שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ,
For the name of any entity indicates the vitality animating it,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּאָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן: "וְכֹל אֲשֶׁר יִקְרָא לוֹ הָאָדָם נֶפֶשׁ חַיָּה הוּא שְׁמוֹ";
as written regarding Adam: 'and whatsoever the man called every living creature, that was its name' (Genesis 2:19);
וַ"אֲגַדְּלָה" לְשׁוֹן גְּדוּלָּה הוּא הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת;
and 'I will make great' (agadlah) from Gedulah signifies expansion;
"וַאֲגַדְּלָה שְׁמֶךָ" – שֶׁתִּהְיֶה הַקְּדֻשָּׁה בְּהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת בְּחַיּוּת בְּלֹא הֶפְסֵק.
meaning: 'and I will make your name great'—that holiness expand continuously in vital life without interruption.
וְהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת מִצַּד אַבְרָהָם עַצְמוֹ עֲדַיִן אֵין בְּטִיחוּת עַל הַקִּיּוּם לָעַד,
And expansion from the vantage point of Avraham himself still offered no guarantee of enduring eternity,
כִּי הָיָה גַּם פְּסֹלֶת בְּזַרְעוֹ,
since dross emerged in his seed (Yishmael),
וְכֵן בַּגֵּרִים שֶׁגִּיֵּיר כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל;
as well as among the proselytes he converted, as noted above;
אֲבָל יַעֲקֹב הוּא "שְׂפַת אֱמֶת תִּכּוֹן לָעַד",
however, Yaakov embodies 'the lip of truth shall be established forever' (Proverbs 12:19),
וְלֹא יָצָא פְּסֹלֶת מִזַּרְעוֹ,
no dross emerging from his offspring,
וּמֵאִתּוֹ נִתְפַּשְּׁטָה קְדֻשַּׁת יִשְׂרָאֵל לְעוֹלְמֵי עַד.
and from him the holiness of Israel expanded eternally.
וְכֵן הַגֵּרִים שֶׁבְּשֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל יְכוּנּוּ,
And likewise converts who are titled by the name of Israel,
הֵם גַּם כֵּן כְּקָטָן שֶׁנּוֹלַד, לִהְיוֹת בָּהֶם גַּם כֵּן כֹּחַ הַקִּיּוּם לָעַד.
are also like newborn infants, possessing within them the enduring power of eternity.
וְזֶהוּ גִּידּוּל הַשֵּׁם, דְּהַיְינוּ הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת הַחַיִּים לִזְכּוֹת לְחַיֵּי עוֹלָם,
And this is the magnification of the name—the expansion of life to merit eternal life,
דְּכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל יֵשׁ לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא וְזוֹכִים לְחַיֵּי עוֹלָם,
for all Israel have a share in the World to Come and merit life eternal,
וְזֶה מִצַּד מִדַּת "אֱמֶת לְיַעֲקֹב",
and this stems from the attribute of 'Truth to Yaakov' (Micah 7:20),
וְקַו הָאֶמְצָעִי הוּא הַמַּמְשִׁיךְ מִן הַקָּצֶה אֶל הַקָּצֶה.
and the Central Pillar (Tiferet) extends from one extreme to the other.

sourceExcerpt.en: This is what they expounded: “I will make your name great”—I will add a heh to your name. It was only a point of the greatness his name would later attain through the addition of heh, when he was told, “Your name shall be Abraham.” Now the blessed God’s promise came that He would later make his name great. “I will make your name great” indicates that this point would then spread in its own holiness. h: I will make your name great

p: וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וַאֲגַדְּלָה שְׁמֶךָ – בְּגִין דִּכְתִיב וּמִמּוֹלַדְתְּךָ",
And this is why it says: ''and I will make your name great'—because it is written 'and from your birthplace',
וְהַיְינוּ דִּכְתִיב: "וּבְחֵטְא יֶחֱמַתְנִי אִמִּי",
reflecting what is written: 'and in sin did my mother conceive me' (Psalms 51:7),
וּמִצַּד זֶה בָּא הַפְסָקַת הַחַיִּים בָּעוֹלָם;
and from that aspect mortality and cessation of life entered the world;

whereas Yaakov our Father, peace be upon him, who reflected Adam before the Fall (as explained numerous times),

p: "וֶהְיֵה בְּרָכָה – מִסִּטְרָא דְאַרְעָא דְיִשְׂרָאֵל",
''And you shall be a blessing—from the side of the Land of Israel,'
וְהַיְינוּ דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁהָיָה מֶרְכָּבָה לְמִדַּת מַלְכוּת שֶׁנִּקְרֵאת "אֶרֶץ";
namely King David, peace be upon him, who was the chariot to Malchut which is termed 'Land';
וְהַבְּרָכָה הִיא מִצִּיּוֹן, כְּמַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "כְּטַל חֶרְמוֹן שֶׁיֹּרֵד עַל הַרְרֵי צִיּוֹן, כִּי שָׁם צִוָּה ה' אֶת הַבְּרָכָה וְגוֹמֵר",
and blessing originates from Zion, as stated: 'As the dew of Chermon that comes down upon the mountains of Zion, for there Hashem commanded the blessing, etc.' (Psalms 133:3),
מִצִּיּוֹן הַיְינוּ כָּל אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל, וְנִקְרֵאת "עִיר דָּוִד",
from Zion meaning the entirety of the Land of Israel, titled 'the City of David',
כִּי לֶעָתִיד תִּהְיֶה כָּל אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל קְדֻשַּׁת צִיּוֹן,
for in the future the entire Land of Israel will attain the sanctity of Zion,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (רֵישׁ פְּסִיקְתָּא): "עֲתִידָה יְרוּשָׁלַיִם לִהְיוֹת כְּכָל אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל".
as written (Pesikta): 'Jerusalem is destined to expand like the whole Land of Israel.'
וְהוּא נֶגֶד מַה דִּכְתִיב: "וּמִבֵּית אָבִיךָ",
And this corresponds to what is written: 'and from your father's house',
וְהַיְינוּ דִּכְתִיב: "הֵן בְּעָווֹן חוֹלָלְתִּי",
which aligns with: 'Behold, I was brought forth in iniquity' (Psalms 51:7),
וְאָמְרוּ (מִדְרַשׁ רַבָּה רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת תַּזְרִיעַ):
and the Sages said (Midrash Rabbah, Parashat Tazria):
"אֲפִילּוּ אִם יִהְיֶה חָסִיד שֶׁבַּחֲסִידִים אִי אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה לוֹ צַד אֶחָד מֵעָוֹן וְכוּלֵי",
'Even if one be the most pious of the pious, it is impossible that he not possess some aspect of iniquity, etc.,'
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁאֵינוֹ נָקִי מֵהֲנָאַת עַצְמוֹ,
meaning that one is not entirely pristine from subtle self-gratification,
וְזֶה מִצַּד עֶטְיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ,
and this derives from the counsel of the serpent,
דְּאִיתָא (שַׁבָּת נה עַמּוּד ב): "יִשַׁי אֲבִי דָוִד דִּמְפָרֵשׁ בֵּיהּ קְרָא שֶׁמֵּת בְּעֶטְיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ",
as taught (Shabbat 55b): 'Yishai father of David, concerning whom Scripture explicates that he died solely on account of the serpent's counsel,'
וְעָלָיו נֶאֱמַר "הֵן בְּעָווֹן" מָלֵא (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב שָׁם);
and regarding him 'in iniquity' is spelled full with a Vav (as noted there);
וּמָשִׁיחַ בֶּן דָּוִד יְתַקֵּן גַּם עֶטְיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ,
and Mashiach ben David will rectify even the counsel of the serpent,
וְיַמְשִׁיךְ הַחַיִּים הָאֲמִיתִּיִּים בָּעוֹלָם, כְּמַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "חַיִּים שָׁאַל מִמְּךָ נָתַתָּה לּוֹ וְגוֹמֵר",
and will draw true life into the world, as stated: 'He asked life of You, You gave it to him, etc.' (Psalms 21:5),

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Tiferet Yosef, Talmud Anthology, Pesachim 6: “This is like the Talmud’s teaching in Sanhedrin: they rise with their defects and are healed. A person will recognize himself: from the sufferings he bore in this world, he now has the power of resurrection. This is the meaning of rising with their defects. They recognize that the lack they experienced in this world was, in its depth, established by the blessed God so that there would appear to be a lack for the sake of His righteousness, giving a person room to accomplish something. In this world the person suffered greatly from it and clarified himself as far as his power could reach. From this he now has healing for the wound of his affliction, as it says, “Each man with his staff in his hand.” “From here is an answer to those who say that resurrection is not taught in the Torah.” My revered grandfather explained that Torah means, as the Zohar says, that which teaches and reveals what was concealed and unknown. This is the meaning of Torah reviving the dead. In the very place where a person previously thought there was absence, and did not recognize that light was present there and that he was then connected to the blessed God, God will illuminate for him that the place itself was full of light without a moment’s interruption. There was never any absence; only from the human perception that God established in this world did absence and concealment seem to exist. All the apparent absence, death, and separation from the blessed God arose from that human perception. Thus they rise with their defects: in the future the blessed God will clarify all this for them. When “He swallows up death forever,” it will become clear that there had never been absence or concealment in Israel, and God will wipe tears from every face. This is the answer to those who say resurrection is not taught in Torah: through Torah a person will recognize that he is the very same person who existed before the resurrection, and that he himself exists now after the resurrection.”

reviewedSourceExcerpt.en: This is like the Talmud’s teaching in Sanhedrin: they rise with their defects and are healed. A person will recognize himself: from the sufferings he bore in this world, he now has the power of resurrection. This is the meaning of rising with their defects. They recognize that the lack they experienced in this world was, in its depth, established by the blessed God so that there would appear to be a lack for the sake of His righteousness, giving a person room to accomplish something. In this world the person suffered greatly from it and clarified himself as far as his power could reach. From this he now has healing for the wound of his affliction, as it says, “Each man with his staff in his hand.” “From here is an answer to those who say that resurrection is not taught in the Torah.” My revered grandfather explained that Torah means, as the Zohar says, that which teaches and reveals what was concealed and unknown. This is the meaning of Torah reviving the dead. In the very place where a person previously thought there was absence, and did not recognize that light was present there and that he was then connected to the blessed God, God will illuminate for him that the place itself was full of light without a moment’s interruption. There was never any absence; only from the human perception that God established in this world did absence and concealment seem to exist. All the apparent absence, death, and separation from the blessed God arose from that human perception. Thus they rise with their defects: in the future the blessed God will clarify all this for them. When “He swallows up death forever,” it will become clear that there had never been absence or concealment in Israel, and God will wipe tears from every face. This is the answer to those who say resurrection is not taught in Torah: through Torah a person will recognize that he is the very same person who existed before the resurrection, and that he himself exists now after the resurrection.

p: וְזֶה שֶׁחוֹתְמִין "מָגֵן דָּוִד" בַּהַפְטָרָה, שֶׁבּוֹ נֶאֱמַר: "וְאַתָּה ה' מָגֵן בַּעֲדִי וְגוֹמֵר";
And this is why we conclude 'Shield of David' in the Haftarah, of whom it is said: 'But You, Hashem, are a shield about me, etc.';
מָגֵן הוּא שֶׁלֹּא יַנִּיחַ שׁוּם דָּבָר רַע לִפְגּוֹעַ בָּאָדָם;
a shield is that which permits no evil harm to touch a person;
וְאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם גַּם כֵּן זָכָה לָזֶה בְּמִלְחֶמֶת הַמְּלָכִים,
and Avraham our Father likewise merited this during the War of the Kings,
שֶׁהָיְתָה כְּדֵי לְהַצִּיל אֶת לוֹט שֶׁהָיָה בוֹ נֶפֶשׁ רוּת.
which was undertaken to rescue Lot who bore the soul of Ruth (the Davidic root).
וְחוֹתְמִין "מָגֵן דָּוִד" בַּהַפְטָרָה שֶׁהוּא לְשׁוֹן סוֹף, מַפְטִירִין.
And we conclude 'Shield of David' in the Haftarah, which connotes the end (maftirin).
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּגְּמָרָא: "יָכוֹל יְהוּ חוֹתְמִין בְּכוּלָּם? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: 'וֶהְיֵה בְּרָכָה' – בְּךָ חוֹתְמִין וְכוּלֵי",
And this is what they taught in the Gemara: 'Might one think they conclude with all of them? Scripture states: 'and you shall be a blessing'—with you they conclude, etc.,'
כִּי עִנְיַן "מָגֵן דָּוִד" גַּם כֵּן מִצַּד אַבְרָהָם,
for the reality of 'Shield of David' likewise stems from Avraham,
שֶׁאָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: "אַל תִּירָא אַבְרָם, אָנֹכִי מָגֵן לָךְ וְגוֹמֵר",
unto whom the Holy One declared: 'Fear not, Avram, I am a shield unto you, etc.' (Genesis 15:1),
שֶׁהָיָה אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ מִתְפַּחֵד שֶׁמָּא נִכְשַׁל בְּאֵיזֶה חֵטְא,
since Avraham was afraid lest he stumbled in some sin,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה: "תֹּאמַר אוֹתָן אֻכְלוּסִין שֶׁהָרַגְתִּי שֶׁמָּא הָיָה בָּהֶם צַדִּיק אֶחָד וִירֵא שָׁמַיִם אֶחָד וְכוּלֵי",
as written in Bereishit Rabbah: 'Can it be that among those legions I killed there was one righteous man or God-fearing man, etc.,'
וְאָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: אַל תִּירָא מִכָּל מִכְשׁוֹל, אָנֹכִי מָגֵן לָךְ,
and the Holy One said to him: Fear no stumbling block, I am a shield unto you,
וּמְסַבֵּב אוֹתְךָ מִכָּל צַד שֶׁלֹּא תִּהְיֶה שְׁלִיטָה לְשׁוּם חֵטְא לִשְׁלוֹט בָּךְ.
surrounding you from every side so that no sin shall have dominion over you.
וּקְדֻשַּׁת דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם וּמָשִׁיחַ גַּם כֵּן מִצִּדְּךָ;
And the sanctity of King David and Mashiach likewise originates from you;
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ: "מָגֵן דָּוִד" בַּהַפְטָרָה, מִצַּד שֶׁהוּא יִהְיֶה הַסּוֹף,
and this explains 'Shield of David' in the Haftarah, because he will be the ultimate culmination,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ג, רמ עַמּוּד ב): "סִיּוּמָא – מַלְכָּא מְשִׁיחָא";
as written in the holy Zohar (III, 240b): 'the culmination is King Mashiach';
אֲבָל עִיקַּר הַהַתְחָלָה הוּא מִצִּדְּךָ, וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ שֶׁאֵין חוֹתְמִין אֶלָּא בָּךְ.
yet the primal beginning is from your side, wherefore they taught that we conclude only with you.
וְזֶה שֶׁמְּרַמֵּז בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ: "'וֶהְיֵה בְּרָכָה' – מִסִּטְרָא דְאַרְעָא דְיִשְׂרָאֵל",
And this is what the holy Zohar hints: ''and you shall be a blessing'—from the side of the Land of Israel,'
שֶׁמְּרַמֵּז עַל מָשִׁיחַ, כְּמַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "כִּי שָׁם צִוָּה ה' אֶת הַבְּרָכָה חַיִּים עַד הָעוֹלָם".
alluding unto Mashiach, as stated: 'for there Hashem commanded the blessing, life forevermore.'

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Kometz HaMinchah 2:32:1: ““You shall be a blessing”—with you they conclude, as the Sages said; and likewise with King David. Abraham is the beginning of creation. “Only three are called fathers”: they are the fathers of the world and the beginning of the recognition of divinity. Abraham is the father of them all, “the father of a multitude of nations.” The title father is included in his name, for father means expansion into branches, the quality of kindness that expands. The Zohar says, “Abba founded the daughter.” As explained elsewhere, Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and David correspond to father, mother, son, and daughter. “The final act was first in thought”: King David, who is the Messiah, is the culmination of creation. Therefore the blessing’s concluding seal with him relates to the beginning of thought. The seal is “Shield.” So too with the festivals: recognition begins at Pesach, the month of spring, when the reception of divinity begins; it concludes at the Festival of Ingathering, Sukkot, a shelter and refuge expressing confidence that God protects the person. This comes after the completion of the summer’s service: King David’s level in the name of Lordship, “I have set God before me always,” like a master before his servant, without casting off the kingdom of Heaven for even a moment. Through this, “Whoever accepts the yoke of Torah has the yoke of government removed from him,” and so forth. He merits kingship, which is complete freedom, and the blessed God shields him.”

The blessing of the patriarchs is one of the long blessings, for some blessings have a long form and others a short form. A short blessing signifies the good that comes from His side; a long one signifies a person drawing out and extending that good further, as in “So may the Lord our God bring us to other appointed times and festivals.” The good that comes from His side is clear, but what a person adds of his own requires clarification. Therefore, in long blessings they instituted a further blessing of the blessed God at the conclusion, to include the good within Him. This is “with you they conclude and not with them”: complete clarification belongs to the mystery of kindness, Abraham’s level, in which there is no impurity. The world’s foundation is built on kindness, as it says, “The world shall be built through kindness” (Psalms 89:3). Although Jacob our father’s quality also contains no impurity, there have already been times when both Isaac’s and Jacob’s qualities were hidden from every living eye. Who was greater than the prophet Jeremiah and Daniel? Yet when concealment intensified, they ceased to say “mighty” and “awesome,” which are Isaac’s and Jacob’s qualities, as the Talmud teaches (Yoma 69b). But they did not cease to say “great,” Abraham’s quality, for the quality of kindness never fails.”

sourceExcerpt.en: “And you shall be a blessing—with you they conclude, and not with them.” The meaning is this. The blessing of the patriarchs is one of the long blessings, for some blessings have a long form and others a short form. A short blessing signifies the good that comes from His side; a long one signifies a person drawing out and extending that good further, as in “So may the Lord our God bring us to other appointed times and festivals.” The good that comes from His side is clear, but what a person adds of his own requires clarification. Therefore, in long blessings they instituted a further blessing of the blessed God at the conclusion, to include the good within Him. This is “with you they conclude and not with them”: complete clarification belongs to the mystery of kindness, Abraham’s level, in which there is no impurity. The world’s foundation is built on kindness, as it says, “The world shall be built through kindness” (Psalms 89:3). Although Jacob our father’s quality also contains no impurity, there have already been times when both Isaac’s and Jacob’s qualities were hidden from every living eye. Who was greater than the prophet Jeremiah and Daniel? Yet when concealment intensified, they ceased to say “mighty” and “awesome,” which are Isaac’s and Jacob’s qualities, as the Talmud teaches (Yoma 69b). But they did not cease to say “great,” Abraham’s quality, for the quality of kindness never fails.
